The Kiss

Gustav Klimt, 1907–1908

Oil and gold leaf on canvas

Embracing lovers in gold leaf and patterned robes on a meadow of flowers.

Use this style

Gustav Klimt, The Kiss, 1907–1908. Belvedere, Vienna. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

The Kiss is the high point of Klimt's golden period. Two lovers embrace at the edge of a flowering meadow, wrapped in robes that are almost pure pattern: black and white rectangles on his, coloured circles and flowers on hers. The square canvas is painted in oil, with layers of gold leaf laid onto it.

Klimt showed it at the 1908 Kunstschau in Vienna, and the Austrian state bought it during the exhibition. It has been in the Belvedere in Vienna ever since. The flat gold background recalls Byzantine mosaics, which Klimt had seen in Ravenna.

How it looks on your photo

Photos take on an olive-gold tone with a fine, flecked texture like gold leaf, and darker areas pick up small rectangular marks. Portraits and warmly lit scenes suit it best. Blues and greens in the photo are mostly replaced by gold.
